newsitem.title: POLAND: Warsaw mulls $100 mln Eurobond to build bridges.
newsitem.headline: Warsaw mulls $100 mln Eurobond to build bridges.

text.p: Warsaw Centre municipality is considering a three-year $100 million eurobond issue to finance the construction and modernisation of two bridges across the Vistula river, a municipality spokeswoman said on Monday.

Malgorzata Gajewska of the Praga Polnoc quarter of Warsaw, where the bridges would stand, told Reuters the first tranche would likely be followed by another, $300 million issue to roll-over the first tranche and pay for further investment.

"To finance the construction of the Swietokrzyski and the modernisation of the Siekierkowski bridges the Warsaw Centre municipality is considering a three-year $100 million eurobond issue," Gajewska said.
"On maturity it would be rolled-over with another, $300 million issue which would also cover interest and provide funds for other investment the municipality plans," she said.
Gajewska said the municipality should decide on all the details of the eurobond issue by June 1997.
"The bulk of financing of the bridge construction would be in 1998, so the decision on the details of the borrowing has to be made by the end of the first half of next year," she said.

Gajewska said the construction of the Swietokrzyski bridge would be managed by the Elektrim trader, which would take as part of the payment a 45 hectare dilapidated riverside area called Port Praski for development into an office, hotel and residential area.

"The construction of the Swietokrzyski bridge is estimated to cost 150 to 190 million zlotys, the value of Port Praski is estimated at about 50 million zlotys -- roughly one third of the value of the bridge," Gajewska said.
"The municipality will have to get the remaining cash from state budget subsidies, its own budget surplus, credit and the eurobonds," she said.
It was not immediately clear whether the eurobond was a variation of the $100 million issue five-year fixed-interest Warsaw considered in February and March this year.
Warsaw Centre, comprising seven districts of the capital, is the richest municipality in Poland with an annual budget surplus of 70 million zlotys.
